name: Post-training: from predictor to assistant
summary: Fine-tuning and reinforcement learning that turn a raw text predictor into a helpful, safer assistant.

text: After reading the whole library, the AI knows a lot but doesn't know how to be helpful yet.
Post-training is like manners and practice lessons: people show it good answers and reward the helpful ones.
D1.analogy: Manners and practice lessons after reading the library.

text: A pretrained model continues text; it doesn't naturally follow instructions.
**Supervised fine-tuning** trains it on example conversations that show the behaviour we want.

**Preference learning** (such as RLHF) trains it to prefer answers people rate higher, and **reinforcement learning with checkable rewards** trains reasoning on problems whose answers can be verified.
D2.analogyBreaks: An apprentice understands why feedback is given. A model only optimises the reward signal, so a flawed reward can teach flattery or shortcuts (reward hacking).

predict.question: A reward model accidentally gives higher scores to longer answers. What will reinforcement learning tend to produce?
predict.explanation: Models optimise what the reward measures, so a length bias in the reward shows up as verbosity: a classic reward-hacking example.

text: Open problems: reward hacking and sycophancy, supervising models on tasks too hard for people to grade, and how much capability comes from post-training versus pretraining.
